intro: Pick the tab or screen you need help with. Each topic walks you through it step by step: a picture of the real screen, a number on every button, and what each one does. Use Back and Next (or the ← → keys); click a picture to see it full size.
note: The pictures come from the app itself, taken with the app’s own sample loans and made-up files (a made-up T12, rent roll and agreement) — never your real tenants. Claude’s answers in the pictures are made-up examples.

chapters.title: A loan’s page
chapters.intro: Open a loan and read its page — the tiles, the rate notice, the NOI box, the Loan Record and the schedule — then add, edit, flag, pool, release and remove loans.

topics.title: Open a loan
topics.intro: Two ways in: click a loan in Portfolio detail on Home, or pick its property under Specific Property.

steps.title: From Home: Portfolio detail
steps.text: Scroll Home down to Portfolio detail. Every loan is a row; click a row and its page opens. A property with two or more loans is one row with a “2 loans” badge — click it to open it, then pick a loan.

marks.label: A loan
marks.text: Click the row: the loan’s page opens (next step).

marks.label: Status
marks.text: The loan’s status: Active, Matured, Extended, Extension undecided (topic “Loan statuses”).

marks.label: A property with 2 loans
marks.text: Click to open or close it. Its row shows the two loans added together.

marks.label: One of its loans
marks.text: Each loan of the property, marked senior or mezz. Click one to open its page.

marks.label: No loan yet
marks.text: A property with no loan sits at the bottom. Clicking it opens it in Underwriting.

marks.label: Top lender
marks.text: The lender with the biggest share of the book.

marks.label: All lenders
marks.text: Show only the loans of the lenders you pick (see the Home chapter).

steps.title: The loan’s page
steps.text: This is the loan’s page. The bar at the top is the same for every property: pick another property, add a loan or a property, edit or archive this property, or open the refinance.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Back to Home’s overview of the whole book.

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: This view: one property and its loans.

marks.label: Select a property
marks.text: Every property, A to Z. Pick one and its page opens. A property with several loans says so (“senior + mezz”); one with no loan says “no loan yet”.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: Opens an empty loan form, with this property’s name filled in (topic “Add a loan”).

marks.label: Add Property
marks.text: Adds a property by its name (see the Properties chapter).

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens this PROPERTY’s profile — its units, manager, NOI override. To change the loan itself, use Edit in the Loan Record.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Archives this PROPERTY with all its loans (it asks first). To remove only one loan, use Remove in the Loan Record.

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: Opens the refinance for this property (see the Refinance chapter).

marks.label: The tiles
marks.text: The loan’s main figures (next topic).

marks.label: Rate notice
marks.text: How a floating or hybrid rate is set this month (topic “The floating-rate notice”).

marks.label: NOI box
marks.text: The property’s NOI and coverage (topic “The NOI box”). Below it: the profile, rent roll, documents, the Loan Record and the schedule — scroll down.

marks.label: Portfolio tab
marks.text: This tab. Tools like Underwriting open in tabs next to it, from the “+”.
Opens Underwriting, the Calendar or Data Health in a new tab.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Back up, restore, and Excel export / import (see the Home chapter).

marks.label: Fetch live rate
marks.text: Gets today’s index values (SOFR, Treasuries, Prime).

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: Display size, the guide and more (see the Settings chapter).

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties are in the book.

topics.title: The tiles
topics.intro: Eight tiles at the top of the page. The app works them out from the loan’s terms — you never type them.

steps.title: What each tile says
steps.text: Each tile is one figure, worked out for today from the Loan Record. Change a term in the Loan Record and the tiles follow at once.

marks.label: Total Monthly Debt Service
marks.text: What goes out each month: principal and interest, plus the escrows and fees in the Loan Record.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: This month’s principal + interest. Underneath: interest-only, the phase of a hybrid, or that it amortizes.

marks.label: Current Balance
marks.text: What is owed today, and how many payments have been made.

marks.label: Original Amount
marks.text: The loan amount on day one, and today’s rate.

marks.label: Amort / Loan Term
marks.text: Amortization years / loan years. “Balloon at mo 120” means the rest is due at month 120.

marks.label: Months to Maturity
marks.text: Months left, and the maturity date.

marks.label: Interest-Only
marks.text: The interest-only months at the start (or “None”), and what follows them.

marks.label: Rate Type
marks.text: Fixed, Floating or Hybrid ARM. A hybrid shows its first rate → its rate after the reset.

topics.title: The floating-rate notice
topics.intro: A floating loan, or a hybrid ARM, has a blue notice under the tiles: how its rate is set this month.

steps.title: A floating loan
steps.text: A floating loan re-prices on the 1st of each month: the index plus the spread (kept between the floor and the cap). Future months use today’s value — the projection holds it flat.

marks.label: How it re-prices
marks.text: When the rate changes and which index it follows.

marks.label: This month’s rate
marks.text: Index + spread = this month’s rate. The floor or cap shows when the loan has one.

marks.label: Captured
marks.text: When this month’s rate was taken. It is automatic — nothing to do.

steps.title: A hybrid ARM
steps.text: A hybrid ARM is fixed for its first years, then floats. The notice says how many fixed months are left — or, once it has reset, that it now floats and how often it resets.

marks.label: Its phase
marks.text: Still fixed (with the months left), or now adjustable.

marks.label: The floating rate
marks.text: What the index + margin is this month.

marks.label: Captured
marks.text: When the index value was taken (automatic).

topics.title: The NOI box
topics.intro: Under the tiles: the property’s NOI and the coverage figures, and where that NOI came from.

steps.title: NOI, DSCR, debt yield, LTV
steps.text: One NOI for the property — the same one Underwriting, Home and the refinance use. The small line says where it came from, in this order: your NOI override (in the profile), else the T12, else the property’s operating lines, else an NOI typed on the loan. With none, it says “No NOI yet”.

marks.label: Property NOI
marks.text: The property’s yearly NOI.

marks.label: DSCR (combined)
marks.text: NOI ÷ the yearly debt service of every loan on the property.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ what is owed today.

marks.label: LTV
marks.text: What is owed ÷ the property’s value (NOI ÷ cap rate).

marks.label: Build operating model
marks.text: Opens this property in Underwriting, where its T12 goes (“Open operating model” once it has one).

marks.label: Where the NOI came from
marks.text: Here: an NOI typed on the loan, no T12 yet. With two loans it adds “shared by 2 loans”.

topics.title: The Loan Record
topics.intro: Every field of the loan in one place, and the buttons that change it.

steps.title: Read the Loan Record
steps.text: Four parts you type (Loan Identification, Loan Terms, Escrows & Reserves, Additional Fees) and one the app works out (Debt Service). A “calc” tag means worked out by the app. A dash means empty.

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens this loan’s form to change any field (topic “Edit a loan”).

marks.label: Out of date…
marks.text: Marks the terms as no longer right — e.g. refinanced, new papers not in yet (topic “Out of date”).

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes this one loan out of every total. It can be restored (topic “Remove a loan”).

marks.label: Loan Identification
marks.text: The property, the lender, the loan number — and for a pooled loan, its other properties and releases.

marks.label: Loan Terms
marks.text: Amount, rate, dates, term, amortization, interest-only and the index. The schedule is built from these.

marks.label: Escrows & Reserves
marks.text: The monthly escrows paid with the loan.

marks.label: Additional Fees
marks.text: Servicing, trustee and other monthly fees.

marks.label: Debt Service (computed)
marks.text: Balance today, P&I, total debt service, interest-only left, months to maturity, today’s rate — all worked out.

marks.label: calc
marks.text: This figure is worked out by the app; it can’t be typed.

topics.title: The payment schedule
topics.intro: At the bottom of the page: every month of the loan, from the first payment to the last.

steps.title: The schedule
steps.text: One row per month. Yellow rows are interest-only, the blue row is today, the green row is the balloon (or the last payment).

marks.label: The loan in one line
marks.text: How many months, when interest starts and ends, and that each month is paid on the 1st of the next.

marks.label: First interest payment
marks.text: Jumps to the first payment and flashes it.

marks.label: First P&I payment
marks.text: Jumps to the first month with principal (after interest-only).

marks.label: Colours
marks.text: What the row colours mean: interest-only, today, balloon / final.

marks.label: Schedule CSV
marks.text: Saves the whole schedule as a file that opens in Excel.
The payment number.

marks.label: Accrual Month / Pays
marks.text: The month interest is counted for, and the day it is paid.

marks.label: Days
marks.text: Days in the month — interest is counted on real days (Actual/360) unless the loan is 30/360.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: That month’s rate. A small tag says where it came from (fixed, the index on a date).

steps.title: Interest-only, then principal
steps.text: “First P&I payment” jumps here: the last interest-only month (IO tag), then the first month that pays principal too. The payment goes up; the balance starts to go down.

marks.label: IO
marks.text: An interest-only month: the payment is interest only.

marks.label: First P&I month
marks.text: From here each payment also pays principal.

marks.label: Rate tag
marks.text: Point at it to see where the rate came from.

marks.label: Interest Charged
marks.text: Balance × rate × days ÷ 360.

marks.label: Scheduled Payment
marks.text: What is due that month.

marks.label: Principal Paid
marks.text: Payment − interest: what comes off the balance.

marks.label: Ending Balance
marks.text: What is owed after that month.

topics.title: Add a loan
topics.intro: Add Loan opens an empty form. Here we add a made-up loan on a made-up property, “Maple Court (example)”.

steps.title: The form
steps.text: Click Add Loan. The form has four parts. Only what you type is kept — the balance, the payments, P&I and debt service are worked out from it. The property you were on is already filled in.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: A new loan. (Editing a loan shows “Edit Loan”.)

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the form. Nothing is saved.

marks.label: Save Loan
marks.text: Checks the form and saves the loan; its page opens.

marks.label: Property Name
marks.text: Filled in with the property you were on. Type another name for another property — a new name makes a new property.

marks.label: Loan Identification
marks.text: Who and what (a step below).

marks.label: Loan Terms
marks.text: The terms from the loan papers.

marks.label: Escrows & Reserves
marks.text: Monthly escrows.

marks.label: Additional Fees
marks.text: Monthly fees.

steps.title: Something missing
steps.text: Save with a required field empty and a red line says what is missing. Nothing is saved until it is right. Required fields have a red *.

marks.label: What is missing
marks.text: The first thing to fix. Fix it and click Save Loan again.

marks.label: Save Loan
marks.text: Try again once it’s fixed.

steps.title: Loan Identification
steps.text: Who and what: the property, its address and type, the lender and the loan number. Here: “Maple Court (example)” with a made-up lender.

marks.label: Property Name
marks.text: The property this loan is on. Start typing to pick one you already have.

marks.label: Property Address
marks.text: Its address. Two loans with the same address are one property.

marks.label: Property Type
marks.text: Office, Retail, Industrial, Multifamily, Mixed-Use or Other.

marks.label: Lender Name
marks.text: Who lent the money.

marks.label: Loan Number
marks.text: The lender’s number for the loan.

marks.label: Pool releases
marks.text: For a pooled loan: properties released so far. Filled in by Release… on the loan’s page — not typed here.

marks.label: Also secures (pooled loan)
marks.text: Leave it empty for a loan on one property. Tick other properties to make one loan on several (topic “A pooled loan”).

steps.title: Loan Terms
steps.text: The terms from the loan papers. A new fixed loan takes its rate from an index + your spread, and the green line shows the rate it will lock. For a loan that already exists, tick “historical loan” and type its rate instead.

marks.label: Historical loan
marks.text: Tick it for a loan that already exists: you type its real locked rate. Leave it off for a new loan.

marks.label: Original Loan Amount
marks.text: The amount on day one. Required.

marks.label: Rate Type
marks.text: Fixed, Floating or Hybrid ARM. The fields below change to match.

marks.label: Lien Position
marks.text: Senior, or Mezzanine (paid after the senior).

marks.label: Loan Status
marks.text: Leave blank: it reads Active, or Matured after the maturity date (topic “Loan statuses”).

marks.label: Origination Date
marks.text: When the loan closed. Required.

marks.label: First Payment Date
marks.text: The first payment of any kind — an interest-only one counts. Required.

marks.label: Maturity Date
marks.text: From the papers. The schedule is anchored to it.

marks.label: Loan Term (Months)
marks.text: Months until the balloon. Required.

marks.label: Amortization Period
marks.text: Months the payment is worked out over, e.g. 360 for 30 years.

marks.label: Day-Count
marks.text: Actual/360 (interest on real days) or 30/360 (the same every month).

marks.label: Amortization Type
marks.text: Level (normal), Fixed Principal, or Fixed P&I (a set payment from the papers).

marks.label: Interest-Only Period
marks.text: Months of interest only at the start. 0 if none.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: The index the rate is built on (SOFR, Prime, a Treasury…).

marks.label: Spread
marks.text: Your margin over the index, in %.

marks.label: Locked rate
marks.text: Index today + spread = the rate this new loan locks.

steps.title: Escrows & Reserves
steps.text: Monthly amounts paid with the loan. Leave any you don’t have empty. They add to Total Monthly Debt Service.

marks.label: Real Estate Tax Escrow
marks.text: Monthly tax escrow.

marks.label: Insurance Escrow
marks.text: Monthly insurance escrow.

marks.label: Replacement Reserve
marks.text: Monthly reserve for replacements.

marks.label: TI/LC Reserve
marks.text: Tenant improvements and leasing commissions reserve.

marks.label: Ground Lease Payment
marks.text: Monthly ground rent, if any.

marks.label: Other Escrow 1 — Description
marks.text: Name another escrow…

marks.label: Other Escrow 1 — Amount
marks.text: …and its monthly amount.

marks.label: Other Escrow 2 — Description
marks.text: A second one.

marks.label: Other Escrow 2 — Amount
marks.text: Its monthly amount.

steps.title: Additional Fees
steps.text: Monthly fees paid with the loan. They also add to Total Monthly Debt Service.

marks.label: Servicing Fee
marks.text: Monthly servicing fee.

marks.label: Trustee Fee
marks.text: Monthly trustee fee.

marks.label: Other Fee 1 — Description
marks.text: Name another fee…

marks.label: Other Fee 1 — Amount
marks.text: …and its monthly amount.

marks.label: Other Fee 2 — Description
marks.text: A second one.

marks.label: Other Fee 2 — Amount
marks.text: Its monthly amount.

steps.title: Saved
steps.text: Click Save Loan. The new loan’s page opens — “Maple Court (example)” is now in the property list — with its tiles worked out. A new property name made a new property, with its own folder for its files.

marks.label: Total Monthly Debt Service
marks.text: P&I + the escrows + the fee typed in the form.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: Interest-only for the first 24 months, then the amortizing payment.

marks.label: Rate Type
marks.text: Fixed at the locked rate.

topics.title: Edit a loan
topics.intro: Edit in the Loan Record opens the same form with the loan’s values. Every change is kept in the loan’s history.

steps.title: Change a field
steps.text: Click Edit in the Loan Record, change what you need, and click Save Loan. Here the made-up lender name is changed.

marks.label: The changed field
marks.text: Type the new value.

marks.label: Property Name
marks.text: A new name renames the property; its files and chats move with it. If that name already has files, the app asks first. For a property with several loans, rename it in its profile.

steps.title: History on a field
steps.text: After saving, a field that was changed shows “history (1)”, and the Loan Record shows “Change history” with every change to this loan.

marks.label: history (1)
marks.text: Click to see this field’s changes.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to this loan, newest first.

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Open the form again.

steps.title: The history window
steps.text: Each change: when, old → new, who made it and where it came from (typed by hand, a rename, the assistant…).

marks.label: Which field
marks.text: The field and the loan.

marks.label: When
marks.text: The day and time of the change.

marks.label: Old → new
marks.text: What it was and what it became.

marks.label: Who
marks.text: Who made the change.

marks.label: Where from
marks.text: Typed by hand, or where else it came from.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the window.

topics.title: Out of date
topics.intro: When a loan’s terms are no longer right — say it was refinanced and the new loan’s papers haven’t come — flag it. Its figures stay as they are, but every place that shows them warns you.

steps.title: Mark it out of date
steps.text: Click “Out of date…” in the Loan Record. Say why, then click Mark out of date. Nothing in the loan is changed.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: A short reason. It shows on the page, the refinance and Needs Attention.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes it; nothing changes.

marks.label: Mark out of date
marks.text: Flags the loan (next step).

steps.title: The warning
steps.text: The loan’s page now has an amber warning under the tiles; so do its refinance and Home’s Needs Attention. When the new loan’s papers come, add the new loan and mark this one Paid off.

marks.label: Out of date
marks.text: Since when, and why. Don’t rely on its figures until the new loan is in.

marks.label: It’s up to date again
marks.text: Clears the flag (it asks first).

steps.title: Clear it
steps.text: “It’s up to date again” (or “Up to date again” in the Loan Record) asks once, then clears the flag. The change is kept in the loan’s history.

marks.label: The question
marks.text: Clear “out of date” on this loan?

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the flag.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Clears it: the warning goes away.

topics.title: Loan statuses
topics.intro: A loan’s status says where it stands. It is a field in Loan Terms.

steps.title: Set a status
steps.text: Edit the loan and pick its Loan Status. Blank reads Active (or Matured once the maturity date has passed). Active — running. Matured — past maturity. Extended — the lender extended it. Extension undecided — waiting on an answer. Paid off — it leaves every total and moves to “Removed & paid-off loans” on Home.

marks.label: Loan Status
marks.text: Here: Extension undecided.

marks.label: Maturity Date
marks.text: With no status set, a loan past this date reads Matured.

steps.title: Where it shows
steps.text: The status shows as a small tag on the loan’s row on Home. Matured and Extension undecided are also highlighted in the maturity calendar and the roll-up.

marks.label: Extension undecided
marks.text: The made-up loan’s new status.

marks.label: Active
marks.text: A loan with no status set, before its maturity.

topics.title: A senior + mezz stack
topics.intro: A property with a senior loan and a mezzanine loan opens as one page that adds them together (the sample Avalon White Plains).

steps.title: The tiles add the loans together
steps.text: In the property list it reads “Avalon White Plains · senior + mezz”. Its tiles add both loans: balance, P&I, debt service. Rate Type shows each loan’s type and the blended rate. The NOI box below says “shared by 2 loans”.

marks.label: Total Monthly Debt Service
marks.text: Both loans together.

marks.label: Current Balance
marks.text: Both balances added.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: Both P&I payments.

marks.label: Rate Type
marks.text: Each loan’s type and the blended rate.

steps.title: Combined position
steps.text: At the top of the Loan Record: each loan, and the stack together. To edit or remove one loan, use the pencil or the bin on its row.

marks.label: The senior loan
marks.text: Click to open only this loan’s page.

marks.label: The mezz loan
marks.text: Click to open only the mezz.

marks.label: Edit this loan
marks.text: Opens this loan’s form.

marks.label: Remove this loan
marks.text: Removes only this loan (it asks first).

marks.label: Combined balance
marks.text: Both balances.

marks.label: Blended rate
marks.text: The rate of the two together, weighted by balance.

marks.label: Combined monthly P&I
marks.text: Both P&I payments.

marks.label: Combined LTV
marks.text: Both balances ÷ the value.

marks.label: DSCR — senior only
marks.text: Coverage of the senior loan alone.

marks.label: DSCR — combined
marks.text: Coverage of both loans.

marks.label: Debt yield — combined
marks.text: NOI ÷ both balances.

marks.label: No NOI yet
marks.text: Without an NOI the coverage figures stay empty.

topics.title: A pooled loan
topics.intro: One loan secured by several properties. Here a made-up loan on “Aspen Yard (example)” also secures “Birch Commons (example)” and a property not in the app yet, “Cedar Point (example)”.

steps.title: Also secures
steps.text: Add the loan on its main property (here from “+ Add the first loan” on Aspen Yard’s page) and fill its terms. Under “Also secures”, tick the other properties. An allocated amount is optional. A property not in the app yet: type its name and click “Add to this loan”.

marks.label: Its main property
marks.text: The loan is filed under this property.

marks.label: How many
marks.text: How many other properties this loan secures.

marks.label: Find a property
marks.text: Type part of a name to shorten the list.

marks.label: Tick a property
marks.text: Ticked: this loan also secures it.

marks.label: Allocated $
marks.text: Optional: the part of the loan the lender puts on this property. If no property has one, each share follows its NOI.

marks.label: New — added when you save
marks.text: A property not in the app yet. It is created when you save the loan.

marks.label: Has its own loan
marks.text: A property can be in a pool and still have its own loan.

marks.label: New property
marks.text: Type the name of a property that isn’t in the app yet…

marks.label: Add to this loan
marks.text: …and click here to add it to the list, ticked.

marks.label: Allocated so far
marks.text: The allocated amounts added up, against the loan amount.

steps.title: The pool panel
steps.text: After Save Loan, the page shows the pool instead of the NOI box: one loan, one payment, and coverage read on the whole pool. Each property has a row (here with made-up NOIs).

marks.label: Pooled loan
marks.text: How many properties secure the loan.

marks.label: Current balance
marks.text: What is owed on the one loan.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: The one payment.

marks.label: Pool NOI
marks.text: Every property’s NOI added.

marks.label: DSCR (pool)
marks.text: Pool NOI ÷ the loan’s yearly debt service.

marks.label: Debt yield / LTV
marks.text: For the whole pool.

marks.label: This property
marks.text: The property whose page this is.

marks.label: Allocated
marks.text: Each property’s part of the loan: the amount typed, or an even split of what is left.

marks.label: Alloc. balance
marks.text: Its part of what is owed today.

marks.label: Alloc. DSCR
marks.text: Each property’s NOI ÷ its share of the debt service.

marks.label: Release…
marks.text: Takes this property out of the pool (next step). Released, the main property moves the loan to the property with the largest share.

steps.title: Release…
steps.text: When a property is sold or refinanced on its own, the lender releases it: its release price is paid down on the loan. It leaves the pool and keeps its NOI, with no loan.

marks.label: Its share
marks.text: Its share of today’s balance — by its allocated amount, or by NOI. Lenders often ask 105–125% of it.

marks.label: Release price
marks.text: What is paid down on the loan.

marks.label: Date
marks.text: The day of the paydown.

marks.label: After the paydown
marks.text: Recalculate the payment over the amortization left, or keep the payment (the loan pays off faster).

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes it; nothing changes.

marks.label: Release
marks.text: Pays it down and takes the property out of the pool.

steps.title: Released
steps.text: The property is gone from the pool, and a line says what was paid down and when. The schedule shows the paydown in its month. Cedar Point stays in the app as a property with no loan.

marks.label: One fewer
marks.text: The pool now secures 2 properties.

marks.label: Released
marks.text: Which property, when, how much was paid down, and whether the payment was recalculated.

steps.title: From a member property
steps.text: A property in the pool with no loan of its own opens with an “In a pooled loan” tag and the same pool panel.

marks.label: In a pooled loan
marks.text: This property secures a pooled loan.

marks.label: + Add the first loan
marks.text: It can still get a loan of its own.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Archives the property (see the Properties chapter).

marks.label: The pool
marks.text: The same panel as on the main property’s page; this property’s row is marked.

marks.label: Profile
marks.text: Its facts (see the Properties chapter).

marks.label: Rent roll
marks.text: Its rent roll summary.

marks.label: Documents
marks.text: Its saved files.

topics.title: At the Reset
topics.intro: A hybrid ARM with a set payment (Fixed P&I) needs one more answer: what the payment does when the rate resets. Shown on a made-up loan, “Juniper Flats (example)”.

steps.title: The At the Reset field
steps.text: It shows when Rate Type is Hybrid ARM and Amortization Type is Fixed P&I. Pick what the note says: keep the stated payment across the reset, or set a new payment — what is owed then, over the amortization left, at the new rate.

marks.label: Hybrid ARM
marks.text: Fixed first, then it floats.

marks.label: Annual Interest Rate
marks.text: The fixed rate of the first years.

marks.label: Fixed P&I
marks.text: A set monthly payment from the papers.

marks.label: Fixed Amortization Payment
marks.text: That set payment.

marks.label: At the Reset
marks.text: Keep the stated payment, or recalculate over the remaining amortization.

marks.label: Initial Fixed Period

marks.label: Cap

marks.label: Spread Over LIBOR

marks.label: Payment before

marks.label: Payment after

marks.label: Reset

marks.label: Payment before

marks.label: New payment

steps.text: Its name with “No loan yet”, its NOI box, its profile, its rent roll and its documents. Removed or paid-off loans, if any, are listed here with Restore. (The profile opens by itself on this page; here it is closed to show the whole page.)

marks.label: Underwriting & Sizing
marks.text: The T12, the underwritten NOI, debt sizing and the pro forma — this chapter.

topics.title: Upload a T12
topics.intro: Two ways: drag the file onto the box, or click “choose a file” and pick it from your computer. Excel and CSV exports are read; the T12 sheet is found by itself.

steps.title: Pick the property first
steps.text: Choose the property in the Property list. The T12 you upload is saved in that property’s folder, and read from there from now on.

marks.text: Or click here: your computer’s file window opens — find the T12, click it, then Open.

steps.title: Read by the reader and the AI
steps.text: The file is saved to the property’s folder and read twice — by the app’s own reader and by Claude — before anything from it is used. When every check passes and both agree, it is used at once; otherwise a window shows you the rows and you decide (the Documents chapter shows that window in full).

marks.label: Setup built
marks.text: The file’s name, and that the table below was built from it.

marks.label: file verified
marks.text: The file was read in full and its totals tie to the statement.

marks.label: Checked by the reader and the AI
marks.text: Both readings agree — the figures are in use.

marks.label: Review the reading

marks.label: Read again

marks.label: NOI used

steps.title: Review the reading
steps.text: Every row of the file as the reader read it: what it is (an account, a category, a total), income or expense, its category in the file, the underwriting line it lands on, the amount used, and a check against its months. You can change any of these, with a note; nothing is saved until you click Save.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: Whether every check passes and the AI agrees with the reader.

marks.label: What the reader made of it

marks.label: Underwriting line
marks.text: The line of the Underwriting table this account adds to.

marks.label: Your note
marks.text: Why you changed a row — kept with the reading.

marks.label: Close without saving

marks.label: Save this reading

steps.title: Units, gross potential rent, average rent
steps.text: The units set the replacement reserve and every per-unit figure. The gross potential rent replaces the statement’s rent in the underwritten column; leave it blank to use the statement’s.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: How many apartments the property has (from the rent roll). Typing it here also asks to save it in the property’s profile.

marks.label: Gross potential rent — per year
marks.text: A year’s rent if every unit were leased at market, before vacancy. Blank = the statement’s rent.

marks.label: Average rent per unit — per month
marks.text: Easier than the yearly figure: the average monthly rent for one unit; the app works out average × units × 12.

topics.title: The underwriting table
topics.intro: Every line of the T12, classified: the statement’s figure (In-Place), the underwritten figure, and each per unit.

steps.title: The three figures on top
steps.text: In-place NOI (the statement, by the T12 rule), the underwritten NOI (the statement re-priced by your assumptions — the figure a loan is sized on) and the largest loan it supports.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The T12’s own NOI — the 12-month total, or the last 3 months × 4 when the statement starts in a lease-up.

marks.label: How it was worked out
marks.text: Which months it comes from.

marks.label: ties to statement NOI
marks.text: The lines add up to the NOI printed on the statement.

marks.label: Underwritten NOI
marks.text: The statement with your vacancy, management fee and reserves — what a lender would size on.

marks.label: Max supportable loan
marks.text: The largest loan that NOI supports at the debt-sizing limits (lower on the page).

steps.title: The columns
steps.text: Every line of the T12, classified (the line names are the app’s; the Documents chapter shows how each account was placed). Two figures per line, each also per unit.

marks.label: Line
marks.text: The underwriting line; a line far from its benchmark is flagged next to its name.

marks.label: In-Place (T12)
marks.text: Each line as the statement shows it.

marks.label: Underwritten
marks.text: Each line after your assumptions — type over it to pin a line (next step).

marks.label: $/unit
marks.text: The figure ÷ the units.

marks.label: Start a pro forma
marks.text: Starts the pro forma column (see the pro forma topics).

steps.title: Pin a line
steps.text: Type a figure in the Underwritten column to pin that line: the NOI and the sizing recompute from it, and the line is tagged “edited” with who and when. The × puts it back to the computed figure.

marks.label: Typed figure
marks.text: Your underwritten Marketing for the year.

marks.label: edited
marks.text: Marks a pinned line; hover to see when.
Back to the computed figure.

marks.label: Benchmark flag
marks.text: A line more than 15% from its per-unit benchmark is flagged, with the dollar gap.

steps.title: The NOI rows
steps.text: Subtotals for rental income, effective gross income and expenses, then the reserves and the Net Operating Income — each in both columns and per unit.

marks.label: Effective Gross Income
marks.text: All income after vacancy and other deductions.

marks.label: Total Operating Expenses
marks.text: Every expense line added up.

marks.label: Replacement Reserves
marks.text: Your reserves per unit × units — underwritten only (the T12 has none).

marks.label: Net Operating Income
marks.text: In-place and underwritten NOI, and per unit.

topics.title: Assumptions and benchmarks
topics.intro: The three assumptions that turn the statement into the underwritten NOI, and the per-unit benchmarks that flag a line — all per property.

steps.title: Assumptions, benchmarks, save
steps.text: Change an assumption and every underwritten figure, the sizing and the pro forma suggestions follow. Each change is kept in the property’s history.

marks.label: Vacancy
marks.text: The vacancy you underwrite (the better of this and what the statement really runs is used).

marks.label: Management fee
marks.text: As a % of effective gross income (again the better of this and the statement’s).

marks.label: Reserves / unit
marks.text: Replacement reserves a year per unit.

marks.label: Payroll / unit
marks.text: Your payroll benchmark for this property; a payroll line 15% off it is flagged.

marks.label: R&M / unit
marks.text: Your repairs & maintenance benchmark.

marks.label: Save to property record
marks.text: Saves the assumptions and benchmarks with the property, so every screen uses them.

topics.title: Debt sizing
topics.intro: The largest loan the underwritten NOI supports, at the limits you set for this property.

steps.title: Limits and results
steps.text: Each limit gives a loan amount; the smallest one is the maximum supportable loan, and the limit that sets it “binds”.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Max LTV
marks.text: The loan as a share of that value.

marks.label: Min DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ the yearly payment must be at least this.

marks.label: Min debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ the loan must be at least this.

marks.label: Interest rate
marks.text: The rate the payment is worked out at.

marks.label: Amortization
marks.text: Years the payment pays the loan down over.

marks.label: Est. value
marks.text: NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Loan @ LTV
marks.text: What the LTV limit allows.

marks.label: Loan @ DSCR
marks.text: What the coverage limit allows.

marks.label: Loan @ debt yield
marks.text: What the debt-yield limit allows.

marks.label: Max supportable
marks.text: The smallest of the three.

marks.label: Binds on
marks.text: The limit that sets it.

marks.label: Implied ratios
marks.text: The LTV, DSCR and debt yield at the max loan.

topics.title: Operating history and the roll-up
topics.intro: The property’s months kept from every T12, and the whole portfolio’s NOI and coverage in one table.

steps.title: General Data — operating history
steps.text: Every T12 you upload adds its months (up to 24 are kept). Each line shows its trailing 12 months and the change against the 12 before.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The same NOI as everywhere in the app, and how it was worked out.

marks.label: Underwritten NOI
marks.text: With your assumptions.

marks.label: Saved to the folder
marks.text: Kept in the property’s folder (general-data.json).

marks.label: Trailing 12-mo
marks.text: Each line’s last 12 months, and its change.

steps.title: Portfolio roll-up
steps.text: Every property: units, loans, in-place and underwritten NOI, balance, yearly debt service, DSCR, debt yield, LTV and maturity — with the total row. Click a property to underwrite it.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: Each property’s NOI.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ its yearly debt service.

marks.label: A property
marks.text: Click it to open it here.

topics.title: What to push
topics.intro: Claude reads the T12 against your assumptions and benchmarks and ranks what to push to raise the NOI.

steps.title: Claude’s ranked moves
steps.text: It runs by itself once a T12 is read (Claude must be connected), and again when the T12 or the assumptions change. Each move has an estimated NOI impact and an effort.

marks.label: Re-analyse
marks.text: Asks Claude again.

marks.label: A move
marks.text: What to do, why (from this statement’s own figures) and the effort.

marks.label: Estimated NOI impact
marks.text: Claude’s estimate, grounded in the statement — a starting point, not advice.

topics.title: Pro forma — start it
topics.intro: The pro forma is the NOI you show the lender: the T12 with your changes, each with its reason, adding up to the dollar. It is the draft of the underwriting.

steps.title: Start a pro forma
steps.text: Nothing changes until you start it.

marks.label: Start a pro forma
marks.text: Adds the Pro forma column next to Underwritten. It starts equal to the T12 column.

steps.title: The Pro forma column and its bar
steps.text: A third column, Pro forma, with its $/unit. Lines with an amber dot have a suggestion from your assumptions; a teal dot marks a line you changed.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive
marks.text: Which version the column shows (next topic).

marks.label: The two NOIs
marks.text: Safe and Aggressive pro forma NOI.

marks.label: Suggestions
marks.text: Every open suggestion in one list.

marks.label: Revenue credit…
marks.text: Annualize all revenue accounts at once (its own topic).

marks.label: + Add an account
marks.text: An account the T12 doesn’t have (its own topic).

marks.label: For the lender…
marks.text: The Excel file for the lender.

marks.label: History
marks.text: Every pro forma change, with its story.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Removes the pro forma (its history stays).

marks.label: Pro forma · Safe
marks.text: The column. Click any figure in it to open that line’s accounts.

marks.label: Amber dot
marks.text: This line has a suggestion waiting.

topics.title: Pro forma — Safe and Aggressive
topics.intro: Two versions. Safe: what you would defend line by line. Aggressive: Safe plus the changes a cautious lender may not accept.

steps.title: Two versions
steps.text: Aggressive starts as Safe and adds its own changes; a change made for Aggressive on an account wins over Safe’s in Aggressive. Every change says where it applies: Safe, Aggressive or Both. Use the switch to see either one in the column.

marks.label: Safe
marks.text: The column shows the Safe version.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: The column shows the Aggressive version.

marks.label: Both NOIs
marks.text: The one shown first, then the other.

steps.title: How each one adds up
steps.text: Under the table, one box per version: the T12 NOI, every change grouped by its kind with its story, and the pro forma NOI — checked to the dollar.

marks.label: Safe — how it adds up
marks.text: T12 NOI + each change = the Safe pro forma NOI.

marks.label: Aggressive — how it adds up
marks.text: The same for Aggressive.

marks.label: reconciles to the dollar
marks.text: The changes add up exactly (worked out twice).

topics.title: Pro forma — a line’s accounts
topics.intro: Click a figure in the Pro forma column: a window opens with every account of that line.

steps.title: Every account, every month
steps.text: The window is about 80% of the screen. On top, the line in the T12, Underwritten, Safe and Aggressive. Below, every account of the line — none hidden, a $0 one too — with its 12 months as the statement shows them.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: T12, Underwritten, Pro forma Safe and Aggressive for the whole line, each per unit.

marks.label: An account
marks.text: Its row in the file, its 12 months, its T12, Safe and Aggressive. Click it to change it.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: The account’s year in the statement.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive
marks.text: The account in each version.

marks.label: A $0 account
marks.text: Shown with its twelve zeros — nothing is hidden.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: Each month and each column added up.

marks.label: + Add an account the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: For money the statement has no account for.
Closes the window.

topics.title: Pro forma — change an account
topics.intro: Click an account and its choices open right under it. Each change has a kind, the version it applies to and a story.

steps.title: The choices
steps.text: New amount (0 takes the account out), Spread over years, Annualize, % of revenue and Per unit. The next topics show each one.

marks.label: New amount
marks.text: Type the account’s new yearly figure. Type 0 to take it out — it reads “Took out” for the lender.

marks.label: Spread over years
marks.text: A cost paid once every few years counts only its share for one year.

marks.label: Annualize
marks.text: The account becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months.

marks.label: % of revenue
marks.text: The account set as a % of revenue (expenses and rental deductions).

marks.label: Per unit
marks.text: A dollar figure per apartment per year × the units.

steps.title: A new amount, its kind and its story
steps.text: Snow removal set to $9,000 for a normal winter. Pick the kind, where it applies, and write the story the lender reads — or pick one you already wrote. The preview shows the account’s 12 months before and after, the line and the NOI.

marks.label: Its new amount
marks.text: The yearly figure for this account.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Why it changes: non-recurring, spread, normalized, operating change, market norm, partnership/back-office (and revenue credit when annualizing income).

marks.label: Apply to
marks.text: Safe, Aggressive or Both.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads. Required.

marks.label: Draft it with Claude
marks.text: Claude writes a first draft from the account’s months; you edit it.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: The account’s 12 months in the T12 and after the change (each month in proportion).

marks.label: ready to save
marks.text: Or what is still missing.

marks.label: Save the change
marks.text: Saves it; the window stays open on this line.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the choices without saving.

steps.title: Saved
steps.text: The account shows its new figure in Safe and Aggressive, and a tag with where it applies and its kind. The line’s totals follow.

marks.label: The changed account
marks.text: Now 9,000 in Safe and Aggressive; at the right end of its row, a tag says where it applies and its kind (hover it for the story).

marks.label: The line
marks.text: Now $27,500 in both versions.

steps.title: Edit or remove a change
steps.text: Click a changed account again: its changes are listed on top, each with Edit and Remove, who made it and when.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, kind, story, who and when, and its effect on the NOI.

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens it with its figures to change.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Removes it (asks first); the history keeps it.

steps.title: Same story as…
steps.text: One cause often moves several accounts. Pick a story you already wrote and it fills in — then adjust it if you want.

marks.label: Same story as…
marks.text: The stories already in this pro forma, with their account.

topics.title: Pro forma — spread, annualize, % of revenue, per unit
topics.intro: The other ways to change an account.

steps.title: Spread over years
steps.text: For a cost paid once every few years that landed in this T12. Exterior painting cost $14,400 in May and is done every 5 years: the pro forma counts $14,400 ÷ 5 = $2,880 a year. It divides the whole account — for an account that mixes normal monthly costs with one big bill, use New amount instead.

marks.label: Paid every … years
marks.text: How often it is paid; it counts one share a year.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Set to “Spread over years” by itself.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: $14,400 in May becomes $2,880 for the year.

steps.title: Annualize
steps.text: When an account runs differently in its recent months — a new contract, a rent increase — it becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months. Each choice shows what it gives; the last 12 months on a normal 12-month T12 is the T12 itself, so it is greyed (“same as the T12”).

marks.label: Last 3 months
marks.text: × 4 — here $28,400 a year.

marks.label: Last 12 months
marks.text: Only different from the T12 when the file has more than 12 months, or the T12 rule used the last 3 months × 4.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: The months it comes from.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Operating change for an expense; Revenue credit for an income account.

steps.title: % of revenue
steps.text: The account set as a % of revenue: an expense as a % of that version’s effective gross income, a rental deduction (vacancy, bad debt) as a % of gross potential rent. Because you chose it, it moves when that version’s revenue moves — the management fee never moves by itself.

marks.text: The percentage.

marks.label: It follows revenue
marks.text: Only because you picked % of revenue.

marks.label: The management fee
marks.text: Stays at the T12 unless you change its account.

steps.title: Per unit
steps.text: A dollar figure per apartment per year, times the units (120 here) — for a cost quoted per unit, like a maintenance role or turnover.

marks.label: $ per unit a year
marks.text: × the property’s units.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: Here only in the Aggressive version.

marks.label: Preview
marks.text: Safe unchanged; Aggressive $300 × 120 = $36,000.

topics.title: Pro forma — suggestions from your assumptions
topics.intro: The pro forma is the draft of the underwriting: when a line runs above your assumption, its biggest account gets a suggestion with a ready story. Nothing is applied by itself.

steps.title: A suggestion on the account
steps.text: The management fee runs 3% of revenue; your assumption is 2.5%. Its account carries a “Suggested” chip; open it to see the suggestion and why.

marks.label: Suggested
marks.text: A suggestion is waiting on this account.

marks.label: The suggestion
marks.text: The change, its kind, the default story and why.

marks.label: Use this
marks.text: Fills the change and its story in — you can still edit before saving.

marks.label: Not this one
marks.text: Sets it aside (you can bring it back).

steps.title: Every suggestion in one list
steps.text: The “suggestions” button in the bar lists every open suggestion — from your assumptions and from Claude — each with “Open the account”.

marks.label: A suggestion
marks.text: Where, what and its story.

marks.label: Open the account
marks.text: Opens the line with the suggestion filled in.

topics.title: Pro forma — Claude’s stories
topics.intro: In What to push: Claude reads every account month by month and suggests changes a lender would accept.

steps.title: Stories for the pro forma
steps.text: Each card: the line and the account, the change and its kind, the story, how Claude got the number and what you need to back it with the lender, and what it does to the NOI. Claude may not invent an event or a figure; where a story rests on a fact it can’t see, it says what you must confirm.

marks.label: Find stories / Look again
marks.text: Asks Claude (it needs Claude connected).

marks.label: A story
marks.text: One account, one change, its story.

marks.label: How Claude got the number
marks.text: From the statement’s own figures.

marks.label: To back it
marks.text: What you need on hand to prove it.

marks.label: Put it in the pro forma draft
marks.text: Opens the account with it filled in, to check and save.

marks.label: In the pro forma ✓
marks.text: Already in.

topics.title: Pro forma — add an account
topics.intro: For money the T12 has no account for — a PILOT tax, an antenna lease, bad debt at a market norm.

steps.title: Pick the line
steps.text: “+ Add an account” in the bar lists every line — the ones in your T12 first, then the ones it doesn’t have.

marks.label: A line the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: Adding an account here adds the line to the pro forma.

steps.title: Name it, its amount, its story
steps.text: Name the account, give its amount (or % of revenue, or per unit), the kind, where it applies and the story.

marks.label: Account name
marks.text: What the lender will see.

marks.label: Its amount
marks.text: A year’s figure.

marks.label: Preview
marks.text: Nothing in Safe; $500 a month in Aggressive.

topics.title: Pro forma — revenue credit
topics.intro: Every revenue account annualized at once from its last 3, 6 or 12 months — when the property runs better now than the year shows.

steps.title: Revenue credit
steps.text: Each revenue account becomes its last 3 months × 4 (or 6 × 2). The table shows every revenue line month by month, the months used highlighted, the T12 and the annualized figure; today’s occupancy from the rent roll if there is one. A story is required. The management fee does not follow it.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive (its own)
marks.text: Aggressive can have its own; until then it uses Safe’s.

marks.label: T3 / T6 / T12
marks.text: How many recent months. T12 changes nothing on a normal 12-month file.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: Which months.

marks.label: Annualized
marks.text: Each line after the credit.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads.

marks.label: Save the revenue credit
marks.text: Saves it.

topics.title: Pro forma — the result, the lender file, history
topics.intro: The column and how it adds up after the changes; the Excel file for the lender; every change’s history.

steps.title: The column after the changes
steps.text: Changed lines are outlined with a teal dot; hover one to see its kinds. The NOI rows follow.

marks.label: A changed line
marks.text: Teal dot: this line has changes.

marks.label: Pro forma NOI
marks.text: In the NOI row.

steps.title: How it adds up
steps.text: T12 NOI + the revenue credit + each account change, grouped by kind with its story = the pro forma NOI, for Safe and for Aggressive.

marks.label: Revenue credit
marks.text: The credit’s effect.

marks.label: Normalized
marks.text: Snow removal, with its story.

steps.title: For the lender — the Excel file
steps.text: Safe only, or Safe and Aggressive. The file has four sheets: Pro forma (each line with its change, kind and story), Changed accounts, Reconciliation and Monthly (the months used for the revenue credit marked).

marks.label: Safe only
marks.text: One version.

marks.label: Safe and Aggressive
marks.text: Both, side by side.

marks.label: Save the Excel file…
marks.text: Asks where to save “<property> — Pro forma — <date>.xlsx”.

steps.title: History
steps.text: Every pro forma change, edit, removal and set-aside, newest first: which line and account, old → new, the kind and story, who and when.

marks.label: An entry
marks.text: One change with its story.
Closes it.

chapters.title: Maturity & Reset Calendar
chapters.intro: Every balloon (maturity), ARM rate reset and interest-only step-up in the book — as a list or month by month — with the loans that need a maturity decision on top. Click any event to open its loan.

topics.title: Open the calendar
topics.intro: The calendar opens in its own tab, from the “+” at the end of the tab strip.

steps.title: The “+” menu
steps.text: Click the “+” at the end of the tab strip, then “Maturity & Reset Calendar”.

marks.text: Opens this menu: a tool in a tab of its own.

marks.label: Maturity & Reset Calendar
marks.text: Opens the calendar (this chapter). If it is already open, it takes you to its tab.

steps.title: The Calendar tab
steps.text: The calendar is built from every active loan in the book (an archived property, a removed or paid-off loan is left out) and is redrawn whenever a loan changes. Your view and filters stay as you left them while the tab is open.

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the portfolio. The calendar tab stays open.

marks.label: Calendar
marks.text: This tab.

marks.label: Pop out
marks.text: Opens the calendar in a window of its own — handy on a second screen. Clicking an event there still opens the loan here.

marks.label: Close tab
marks.text: Closes the calendar. Nothing is lost — it is rebuilt from the loans next time.

marks.label: Maturity & Reset Calendar
marks.text: The title, and the day it was built (today).

marks.label: The tool bar
marks.text: List or Calendar, the filters, Sort, Clear and Print (the “Narrow it down” topic).

marks.label: Needs a maturity decision
marks.text: Loans that have matured or whose extension is undecided — always on top.

marks.label: The four tiles
marks.text: The totals at a glance; each tile is also a filter.

marks.label: Maturity wall
marks.text: How much debt comes due each year.

topics.title: What’s coming up
topics.intro: The List view, from the top: the decisions, the four tiles, the maturity wall and every event in date order.

steps.title: Needs a maturity decision
steps.text: A red box on top lists every loan that needs a decision about its maturity: a loan whose status is “Matured” (set by hand, or by itself once the maturity date has passed) or “Extension undecided” (set by hand in the loan’s edit form, Loan Status). It stays here — even after the date has passed — until you change the status (Extended, Paid off…).

marks.label: Needs a maturity decision (2)
marks.text: How many loans wait for a decision.

marks.label: Extension undecided
marks.text: The loan’s status: an extension is being discussed and not yet settled.

marks.label: Matured
marks.text: The loan has reached its maturity (or you marked it so) and is not extended or paid off yet.

marks.label: The loan
marks.text: Click the row to open that loan’s page.

marks.label: Date · balloon
marks.text: Its maturity date and the balloon (what is left to pay then).

steps.title: The four tiles
steps.text: Four totals over the loans the filters let through. Click a tile and the list below shows exactly the loans it counts; click it again to show everything.

marks.label: Debt maturing (shown)
marks.text: The balloons of every maturity in the calendar added up, and how many there are.

marks.label: Maturing (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Loans whose maturity falls within the next 12 months.

marks.label: ARM resets (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Adjustable-rate loans whose rate (and payment) changes within 12 months.

marks.label: IO step-ups (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Loans whose interest-only period ends within 12 months — the payment steps up to principal and interest.

steps.title: Maturity wall
steps.text: Debt coming due by year: one bar per year, as long as that year’s balloons. This year’s and next year’s bars are red.

marks.label: The year
marks.text: Each year with at least one maturity.

marks.label: A red bar
marks.text: Coming due this year or next — the closest refinancings.

marks.label: A green bar
marks.text: A later year. The longest bar is the year with the most debt maturing.

marks.label: The amount
marks.text: The total of that year’s balloons.

steps.title: Upcoming events
steps.text: Every event in date order, grouped by year. A row within the next 12 months has a yellow background; a loan needing a maturity decision has a pink one. Click any row to open that loan.

marks.label: Date
marks.text: The day of the event: the maturity date, the payment date the new rate starts, or the first full payment after interest-only.

marks.label: Event
marks.text: Maturity (red), ARM reset (amber) or IO ends (green).

marks.label: Loan
marks.text: The loan.

marks.label: Amount
marks.text: The balloon for a maturity; the balance at that date for a reset or an IO step-up.

marks.label: Detail
marks.text: In words: the balloon due, the new rate and payment, or the new P&I payment.

marks.label: Year
marks.text: Where each year’s events start.

marks.label: Within 12 months
marks.text: A yellow row is less than a year away.

marks.label: The kind of event
marks.text: Maturity, ARM reset or IO ends.

marks.label: Needs a decision
marks.text: A pink row: the loan matured or its extension is undecided — its status is shown next to the event.

topics.title: Month by month
topics.intro: The Calendar view: one box per year; open a year to see its twelve months.

steps.title: The Calendar view
steps.text: Click “Calendar” in the tool bar. The first year with events is open; the others are closed. Each event is a small card in its month, edged in its colour.

marks.label: List
marks.text: Back to the list view.

marks.label: Calendar
marks.text: This view.

marks.label: The colours
marks.text: Red = maturity, amber = ARM reset, green = interest-only ends.

marks.label: A year
marks.text: The year, how many events and how much matures. Click it to close or open its months.

marks.label: A month
marks.text: The month’s events. An empty month says “—”.

marks.label: An event
marks.text: The loan, the kind of event and the amount. Point at it to read the detail; click it to open the loan.

steps.title: Open another year
steps.text: Click a closed year’s line to open its twelve months; click an open one to close it. Several years can be open at once.

marks.label: A closed year
marks.text: ▸ = closed. Click to open it.

marks.label: An open year
marks.text: ▾ = open: its twelve months are below.

marks.text: A loan that matured or whose extension is undecided is marked in red (or amber) with a warning line.
