topics.title: Narrow it down
topics.intro: The tool bar’s filters work in both views and on the four tiles. They stay while the tab is open; Clear removes them all.

steps.title: Lender
steps.text: Click “Lender” for the list of every lender in the book. Tick one or more: only their loans are shown, and the button says how many are ticked.

marks.label: Lender
marks.text: Opens and closes this list.

marks.label: Every lender
marks.text: Tick a lender to show only its loans; tick several to show all of theirs.

marks.label: A tick box
marks.text: On = this lender’s loans are shown.

steps.title: A lender ticked
steps.text: With one lender ticked, the tiles, the wall and the list count only that lender’s loans. Untick it (or click Clear) to see everything again.

marks.label: Lender (1)
marks.text: One lender is ticked.

marks.label: The tiles
marks.text: Now only that lender’s loans.

marks.label: The wall
marks.text: Only that lender’s maturities.

steps.title: Loans
steps.text: Click “Loans” to pick loans by name. Type in the search box to shorten the list, then tick the loans to show.

marks.label: Loans
marks.text: Opens and closes this list.

marks.label: Search loans
marks.text: Type part of a name; only the loans that match stay in the list.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Tick a loan to show only it; tick several to show them together.

steps.title: Amount and Sort
steps.text: Amount keeps only events between a smallest and a largest amount — type 5m for 5 million or 750k for 750 thousand; leave a box blank for no limit. Sort orders the list by date (grouped by year), or by amount, smallest or largest first.

marks.label: Amount — min
marks.text: Smallest amount shown (here 50m = $50,000,000).

marks.label: Amount — max
marks.text: Largest amount shown. Blank = no limit.

marks.label: Sort
marks.text: Date, Smallest amount or Largest amount.

marks.label: Counted again
marks.text: The tiles, the wall and the list count only the events of $50,000,000 or more. Further down, the list is now largest first and not grouped by year.

steps.title: The Sort choices
steps.text: The three ways to order the list.

marks.label: Date
marks.text: By date, earliest first, grouped by year (the usual order).

marks.label: Smallest amount
marks.text: Smallest amount first.

marks.label: Largest amount
marks.text: Largest amount first.

steps.title: Clear and Print
steps.text: Clear removes every filter (lenders, loans, amounts, search and the tile you clicked); the view and the sort stay. Print opens your computer’s print window with the calendar as you see it now — the tool bar is left off the paper.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Removes every filter.

marks.label: Print
marks.text: Prints the calendar (or saves it as a PDF from the print window).

marks.label: Back to blank
marks.text: No filter is on after Clear.

marks.label: Sort stays
marks.text: Clear doesn’t change the order — set Sort back to Date yourself.

steps.title: A tile as a filter
steps.text: Click a tile — here “Maturing (next 12 mo)”. The list switches to just the loans that tile counts, and a line under the tiles says what is shown. Click the tile again, or that line, to show everything.

marks.label: The tile you clicked
marks.text: Outlined while it filters the list.

marks.label: Showing …
marks.text: What the list shows now. Click here to show everything again.

marks.label: Only those loans
marks.text: The rows are exactly the ones the tile counts.

topics.title: Open a loan from an event
topics.intro: Every event — a row in the list, a card in a month, a line in the decision box — opens its loan.

steps.title: Click an event
steps.text: Click any event.

marks.label: An event
marks.text: Click it: the app goes to Portfolio, opens this loan and jumps to that payment in its schedule.

steps.title: The loan, at that payment
steps.text: The app switches to Portfolio, opens the loan and scrolls its amortization schedule to the payment of the event, lit up for a few seconds. The Calendar tab stays open in the tab strip at the top — click it to go back.

marks.label: Amortization Schedule
marks.text: The loan’s payment schedule, on the loan’s page under Portfolio.

marks.label: The payment
marks.text: The schedule row of the event’s date (“pays MM/DD/YYYY”), lit up for a few seconds — here the final payment, the balloon.

chapters.title: Data Health
chapters.intro: One page with what the app knows about every property — and what is missing or needs your look: T12s waiting for review, files waiting for an answer, files without a property, possible duplicates and loans needing a maturity decision.

topics.title: Open Data Health
topics.intro: Data Health opens in its own tab, from the “+” at the end of the tab strip.

steps.title: The “+” menu
steps.text: Click the “+” at the end of the tab strip, then “Data Health”.

marks.text: Opens this menu: a tool in a tab of its own.

marks.label: Data Health
marks.text: Opens Data Health (this chapter). It reads every property’s files first — a moment with a big book.

steps.title: The Data Health tab
steps.text: On top, what needs you: the T12s waiting for review, files waiting for an answer and files without a property (each list only when it has something in it, or a green line when it is clear). Then four numbers, whether every property has its folder, possible duplicates, maturity decisions — and the table of every property at the bottom.

marks.label: Data Health
marks.text: This tab. Pop it out or close it like any tab.

marks.label: Data Health
marks.text: The app version that is running is named under the title.

marks.label: Recompute all figures
marks.text: Works out every property’s figures again from its files (topic “Recompute”).

marks.label: Last recompute
marks.text: When the figures were last worked out, for how many properties, and why (by hand, after an update…).

marks.label: T12s that need your review
marks.text: T12s waiting for you before they are used (topic “T12s waiting for your review”).

marks.label: Files with several parts
marks.text: Workbooks waiting for you to say which part is whose (topic “Files with several parts”).

marks.label: Files without a property
marks.text: Folders no property uses any more (topic “Files without a property”).

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties, and how many active loans.

marks.label: With a T12
marks.text: How many have a T12 in use; the rest are “missing”.

marks.label: Units known
marks.text: How many have their number of units set in the profile; the rest are blank.

marks.label: Need a maturity decision
marks.text: Loans that matured or whose extension is undecided (topic “Maturity decisions”).

marks.label: Properties without a folder
marks.text: Always 0: every property has its folder with its profile and general data. Anything else names the property the app couldn’t make a folder for.

topics.title: T12s waiting for your review
topics.intro: A T12 is read twice — by the app’s reader and by the AI — before it is used. When a check fails or the AI reads it differently, it waits here and nothing from it is used until you decide.

steps.title: The list
steps.text: Every T12 that waits for you, with the property, the file and why. Green and “0” when there is nothing to review. (A T12 read by an older version that passes every check but hasn’t been read by the AI yet is counted on a grey line under the list — it is checked as soon as Claude is connected.)

marks.label: T12s that need your review
marks.text: How many wait for you.

marks.label: A T12 waiting
marks.text: The property · the file — why it waits (here: the AI disagrees on 2 points). Its numbers are not used yet.

marks.label: Review
marks.text: Opens the reading, row by row, to decide (next step).

marks.label: Re-check every T12 now
marks.text: Reads every saved T12 again with the reader and the AI. It shows “Re-checking… 1 of 5” while it works; a T12 that now fails or disagrees is listed here.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Review opens the T12 reading: every row of the file and what the reader made of it, the checks, and where the AI disagrees. Change what is wrong (with a note) and click “Save this reading”, or “Keep it waiting”. The Documents & files chapter shows this window in full.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: Whether every check passes, and whether the AI agrees with the reader.
Closes the window, like Keep it waiting.

marks.label: Income, Expenses, NOI
marks.text: The accounts added up, against the totals the statement prints (✓ when they match).

marks.label: What to look at
marks.text: Each failed check and each point the AI reads differently, with its Excel row — click the row number to jump to it.

marks.label: The rows
marks.text: The file’s own rows, what the reader made of each, and the amounts; you can change any of them.

marks.label: Keep it waiting
marks.text: Closes the window; the T12 stays on this list, unused.

marks.label: Save this reading
marks.text: Saves the reading as it is now; the T12 is used and leaves this list.

topics.title: Files with several parts
topics.intro: A workbook can hold several properties’ statements (one per sheet, or one after another). The app never guesses which part is a property’s own: until you answer, that file’s numbers aren’t used for it.

steps.title: Waiting for your answer
steps.text: Every file with several parts whose part for a property isn’t answered yet. (A file filed before this was asked, matched by its name only, is listed under “Matched by name only — confirm once” with a Confirm button.)

marks.label: Files with several parts waiting
marks.text: How many files wait for an answer.

marks.label: A file waiting
marks.text: The property · the file (how many parts) — its numbers aren’t used until you say which part is its own.

marks.label: Answer
marks.text: Opens the question (next step).

steps.title: Which part is whose?
steps.text: Each part of the file is a line: tick it and pick the property it belongs to. A part can go to any property, several parts to one property (they are added together), or one part to several. Nothing is saved until you approve.

marks.label: Which part of this file belongs to which property?
marks.text: The file, how many parts and sheets — and the property it is asked for.

marks.label: A part
marks.text: Its sheet and name, what it is (T12, rent roll or sheet) and its NOI. Tick it to link it.

marks.label: Tick box
marks.text: On = this part is linked to the property chosen below it.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Don’t link, this property, any other property — or “Add as a new property” named after the part.

marks.label: + another property
marks.text: Adds a second property list: the same part goes to both.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without saving; the file keeps waiting.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Links each ticked part to its property. Each property reads only its own parts — never another’s numbers.

steps.title: A ticked part needs a property
steps.text: Tick a part without picking its property and click Approve: a red line says which part still needs one. Pick the property, or untick the part.

marks.label: Ticked
marks.text: This part is ticked…

marks.label: …but no property
marks.text: …and its property is still “Don’t link”.

marks.label: Pick a property for part 1 — or untick it.
marks.text: What is missing. Nothing was saved.

steps.title: Answered
steps.text: Here part 2 is Sample Oaks’ own: pick it for part 2, untick the others, and Approve. The file leaves the list, and its part goes through the T12 check like any new T12 (it may then wait under “T12s that need your review”).

marks.label: Files with several parts waiting: 0
marks.text: Green: every file’s part is answered.

marks.label: Its part, read
marks.text: Sample Oaks’ part went through the T12 check; here the AI read it differently, so it waits for review like any T12.

topics.title: Files without a property
topics.intro: A folder of files that no property uses any more (left behind by a rename in an older version). The list shows only when there is one.

steps.title: The list
steps.text: Each folder: the name it was saved under and its files. Attach them to the property they belong to, or delete them.

marks.label: Files without a property
marks.text: How many folders belong to no property.

marks.label: The old name
marks.text: The property name the files were saved under.

marks.label: Its files
marks.text: How many, and the first few names.

marks.label: attach to
marks.text: The property to move them to.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Moves the files into that property’s folder (asks first).

marks.label: Delete
marks.text: Deletes the files (asks first).

steps.title: Attach — the question
steps.text: Attach asks first. The files move into the chosen property’s folder; a file with the same name there is kept as a copy, never replaced.

marks.label: Attach these files to …?
marks.text: The property you picked.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: Where the files go.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is moved.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Moves them; the list is drawn again without that folder.

steps.title: Delete — the question
steps.text: Delete asks first too. The files belong to no property, so deleting them changes no figure; the automatic backups still keep a copy.

marks.label: Delete the files of …?
marks.text: The old name.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: It can’t be undone here; the automatic backups keep a copy.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is deleted.

marks.label: Delete
marks.text: Deletes the folder; the list is drawn again.

topics.title: Possible duplicate properties
topics.intro: Two properties that may be one building entered twice: the same street address and city — or, when one has no address, nearly the same name (ignoring capitals, punctuation and words like “The” or “Apartments”). They are never merged by themselves.

steps.title: The list
steps.text: Each pair and why it is listed. If two names are one building, rename one to match so they become one property; if not, click “Not a duplicate”.

marks.label: Possible duplicate properties
marks.text: How many pairs.

marks.label: The pair
marks.text: The two property names.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Same street address and city, or similar names when one or both have no address.

marks.label: Not a duplicate
marks.text: Remembers that these two are different buildings: the pair is not shown again (here or in Settings).

steps.title: Not a duplicate
steps.text: After “Not a duplicate” the pair is gone. With no pair left, a green line says how many distinct properties and loans there are.

marks.label: No duplicate properties detected
marks.text: Every property is distinct (the pairs you marked are left out).

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: Both stay as two properties — nothing was merged.

topics.title: Maturity decisions
topics.intro: Loans that matured, or whose extension is undecided — set in the loan’s edit form (Loan Status), or “Matured” by itself once the maturity date has passed.

steps.title: Loans needing a maturity decision
steps.text: A red list of each such loan with its status. It goes when you change the loan’s status (Extended, Paid off…). The Maturity & Reset Calendar shows the same loans on top.

marks.label: Loans needing a maturity decision
marks.text: How many.

marks.label: Extension undecided
marks.text: An extension is being discussed and not settled.

marks.label: Matured
marks.text: Past (or marked at) its maturity, not extended or paid off yet.

topics.title: Every property
topics.intro: The table at the bottom: one row per property with its T12, units, NOI, when its figures were worked out and its warnings. Properties missing a T12 or units come first.

steps.title: The columns
steps.text: Read across a row to see what the app knows about that property.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Its name (how many loans if more than one) and whether its profile is complete — or what it still needs.

marks.label: Status
marks.text: Worked out from its data: Stabilized, No T12 yet, No loan data yet or Third-party managed.

marks.label: T12 / NOI basis
marks.text: How the NOI is taken from the T12 (12-month total, last 3 months × 4…) and how many months of history.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: From the property’s profile.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The NOI the app uses for it.

marks.label: Computed
marks.text: When its figures were last worked out, and by which app version (red when an older version).

marks.label: Warnings
marks.text: no T12, units unknown, NOI ≤ 0, loan matured, extension undecided, figures from an older version — or “ok”.

marks.label: Open
marks.text: Opens Underwriting for that property.

steps.title: Warnings on a row
steps.text: A row with a maturity decision pending, another whose loan has matured, and a made-up property with no loan yet. A property whose figures were worked out by an older version of the app shows “figures from v…” and a red version under Computed — Recompute (last topic) fixes that.

marks.label: extension undecided
marks.text: One of its loans waits for a maturity decision.

marks.label: no T12
marks.text: No T12 in use yet: add one in its Documents or in Underwriting.

marks.label: units unknown
marks.text: Its number of units isn’t set in its profile.

marks.label: In-place NOI —
marks.text: No NOI yet: it comes from the T12.

marks.label: loan matured
marks.text: A loan of this property has matured.

marks.label: No loan data yet
marks.text: A property with no loan (here the made-up “Queens Gate”).

marks.label: Profile
marks.text: “Profile complete”, or what its profile still needs (address, units…).

marks.label: Open
marks.text: Opens Underwriting for this property.

steps.title: Open
steps.text: Open takes you to Underwriting with that property picked, ready for its T12 and figures.

marks.label: Underwriting
marks.text: Opened (or brought forward) by Open.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property whose Open you clicked.

marks.label: Waiting for your review
marks.text: Its T12 still waits — Review opens the same window as in Data Health.

topics.title: Recompute
topics.intro: Every figure from a T12 is kept with the property and worked out again when the app is updated. Recompute does it now, by hand.

steps.title: Recompute all figures
steps.text: Click it: the button reads “Recomputing…” while every property’s figures are worked out again from its saved files, then the page is drawn again and the line under the button says when, how many and “manual”. Use it after changing files outside the app, or when the Computed column shows an older version.

marks.label: Recompute all figures
marks.text: Works everything out again.

marks.label: Last recompute … · manual
marks.text: When, how many of the properties, and the reason (manual = this button).

chapters.title: The Assistant (Claude)
chapters.intro: Ask Claude about your loans and properties, or ask it to do things in the app. It reads your data and the files you give it, and every change it proposes waits on a card for your Approve.

topics.title: Open the assistant
topics.intro: The Assistant button sits at the bottom right of every screen.

steps.title: The Assistant button
steps.text: Click Assistant (bottom right) on any screen. The chat opens over the app; whatever you were doing stays as it was underneath.

marks.label: Assistant
marks.text: Opens the chat with Claude.

steps.title: The chat window
steps.text: A new chat starts with a few example questions. Everything you need is on this one window: what to ask about, the question box, and the buttons on top.

marks.label: Compact
marks.text: Shortens a long chat into a summary that keeps the facts, so Claude stays quick. Your messages stay saved.

marks.label: New chat
marks.text: Starts a fresh conversation. The current one is kept in History; nothing in your loans changes.

marks.label: History
marks.text: Your saved conversations — open, search, rename, pin or delete them.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the window. The chat stays as it is for next time.

marks.label: Connection
marks.text: Green: Claude is connected and ready. Amber: it isn’t — see “Connection settings” below.

marks.label: Example question
marks.text: Click one to ask it straight away.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Point the chat at one property (or keep it general). Claude reads that property’s saved files first, and files you attach are saved to it.

marks.label: Model
marks.text: Which Claude model answers. “Automatic” lets your subscription choose; the others are the models it offers.

marks.label: Effort
marks.text: How hard Claude thinks: Low is fastest, Max reasons the deepest (a little slower). High is the default.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Adds files to the message — PDF, Word, Excel, text or pictures. They are read on your computer.

marks.label: Message
marks.text: Type your question or what you want done. Enter sends; Shift+Enter starts a new line.

marks.label: Send
marks.text: Sends the message. While Claude works this button turns into Stop.

marks.label: Connection settings
marks.text: How the app connects to Claude: your Claude subscription or an API key.

topics.title: Ask a question
topics.intro: Claude answers from your own loans and properties — the same figures the app shows.

steps.title: Type the question
steps.text: Type in the message box at the bottom, then click Send (or press Enter).

marks.label: Your question
marks.text: Plain words are fine — name a property, a lender or a date.

marks.label: Send
marks.text: Sends it to Claude.

steps.title: The answer
steps.text: Your question shows on the right, Claude’s answer on the left. Ask a follow-up in the same box — the chat remembers what was said.

marks.label: Your message
marks.text: What you asked.

marks.label: Claude’s answer
marks.text: Worked out from the app’s own figures. It never makes up a number — when something is missing it says so.

marks.label: Follow-up
marks.text: Ask the next question here; the conversation carries on.

topics.title: Focus on a property
topics.intro: Pick a property and the chat is about it: Claude reads its saved documents first, and what you attach is saved to it.

steps.title: Pick the property
steps.text: Choose a property in the list under the chat. “No property — general chat” is for the whole portfolio. A chat started on a property is saved with that property.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property this chat is about. Opening the assistant from a loan’s page picks that loan’s property for a new chat.

marks.label: Its documents
marks.text: How many of the property’s saved documents Claude can read.

topics.title: Ask it to do something — the Approve card
topics.intro: Claude can add properties, fill in details, edit loans, import files, run a refinance and more — but nothing changes until you approve its card.

steps.title: Attach a document
steps.text: Click the paperclip and pick the file (here a made-up property summary). It shows above the message box; it is read on your computer and sent with your message.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Opens your computer’s file window to pick one or more files.

marks.label: Attached
marks.text: The files going with your message, and how much was read from each. The × on a file removes it.

marks.label: Saved files
marks.text: How many files are already saved with this property. When you send, the attached file is saved to it too.

marks.label: What to do
marks.text: Say what you want done with the file.

steps.title: The Approve card
steps.text: Claude proposes the change on a card: each line shows the old value, the new one and where it came from (file, page, quote). Untick a line to leave it out.

marks.label: The card
marks.text: What Claude wants to do, line by line.

marks.label: Tick box
marks.text: Only ticked lines are applied — untick one to leave it out.

marks.label: Old → new
marks.text: The value now (crossed out; “none” when empty) and the value Claude proposes.

marks.label: Where it came from
marks.text: The file, page and quote the value was read from, so you can check it.

marks.label: Approve & apply
marks.text: Makes the change, saved in the field’s history as “Assistant, approved by You”.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is changed; Claude is told you said no.

marks.label: Stop
marks.text: Claude is waiting for your answer. Stop ends its turn and cancels the card — nothing is changed.

steps.title: Approved — and what happened
steps.text: After Approve the card shows what was done (✓) and Claude reports back. Cards that wait for you are never applied by themselves; Stop cancels a waiting card.

marks.label: Done
marks.text: The card is closed: it says what was applied (✓) and what was left out. Its buttons are greyed — a card is used once.

marks.label: Claude’s report
marks.text: Claude is told exactly what happened and says so.

topics.title: Saved chats (History)
topics.intro: Every conversation is saved on its own, grouped by property — reopen one to carry on.

steps.title: The list
steps.text: History lists every saved chat, grouped by property (the property you’re on first, then the portfolio, then the rest). Hover a chat for its buttons.

marks.label: Search
marks.text: Finds words in every saved chat.

marks.label: This property / All
marks.text: Only this property’s chats, or all of them.

marks.label: Back to chat
marks.text: Returns to the conversation you were in.

marks.label: Group
marks.text: The property (or Portfolio) the chats below belong to.

marks.label: A chat
marks.text: Its title (your first question), how many messages and when. Click it to reopen and carry on.

marks.label: Pin
marks.text: Keeps it at the top.

marks.label: Rename
marks.text: Gives it your own title.

marks.label: Delete
marks.text: Deletes the conversation (it asks first).

steps.title: Reopened
steps.text: A reopened chat shows its messages and its cards as they ended (read only — an old card can’t be approved again). Type to carry on where you left off.

marks.label: An old card
marks.text: What was proposed and what you decided.

marks.label: Carry on
marks.text: Your next message continues this conversation.

topics.title: Compact a long chat
topics.intro: A long conversation gets slower. Compact keeps the facts and frees up room.

steps.title: Compacted
steps.text: Click Compact: Claude writes a short brief of the conversation (every property, figure and decision) and carries on from it. The full messages stay in the saved chat.

marks.label: Compact
marks.text: Summarizes the chat so far.

marks.label: The brief
marks.text: What Claude keeps from here on.

topics.title: Connection settings
topics.intro: How the app reaches Claude: your Claude subscription (recommended) or an Anthropic API key.

steps.title: Connected
steps.text: Click “Connection settings” under the Attach button. The Claude connection window shows how the app connects; signed in to your Claude subscription, nothing else is needed. (The same window opens from Settings → Claude connection.)

marks.label: Status
marks.text: Green: connected, and how. Amber: not connected, and what is missing.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Signs this computer out of your Claude subscription. The assistant stops until you connect again.

marks.label: Advanced — API key
marks.text: Opens the API-key choice, for pay-as-you-go use instead of a subscription.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Paste a key from console.anthropic.com. It is kept only on this computer and never shown again.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves the key and switches the app to use it.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes this window.

steps.title: When Claude isn’t connected
steps.text: If Claude isn’t connected the status turns amber, Send is greyed out and the connection choices open inside the chat by themselves.

marks.label: Not connected
marks.text: What is missing, in plain words.

marks.label: Connect with your Claude subscription
marks.text: Opens a small sign-in window that takes you to your browser. When you finish, the status turns green.

marks.label: Automatic
marks.text: Uses your Claude subscription, and an API key if one is saved (recommended).

marks.label: Claude subscription
marks.text: Only the subscription — no API key, no per-use billing.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Only an API key — pay as you go.

marks.label: API key
marks.text: Paste a key here. It is kept only on this computer and never shown again.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves the key; the status re-checks.

marks.label: Send (greyed)
marks.text: Waits until Claude is connected, so a message is never lost.

chapters.title: The shared database
chapters.intro: With the shared database your team works on one copy of the loans, properties and files: you sign in, every change is saved with a reason, and the group’s admin decides who can change what.

topics.title: Sign in, or create an account
topics.intro: With a shared database the app opens on its sign-in screen. Each person has their own account in their organization’s group.

steps.title: The sign-in screen
steps.text: Type your email and password and click Sign in: the app opens on your group’s data.

marks.label: Email
marks.text: The email address of your account.

marks.label: Password
marks.text: Your password.

marks.label: Sign in
marks.text: Opens the app on your group’s loans, properties and files.

marks.label: Create an account
marks.text: For someone new: asks to join your organization’s group.

marks.label: Forgot your password?
marks.text: Emails you a code to set a new password.

marks.label: Minimize
marks.text: Hides the window to the taskbar.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the app.

steps.title: Forgot your password — the email
steps.text: Type your account’s email and click “Email me a code”. A 6-digit code is sent to that address.

marks.label: Email
marks.text: The email of the account whose password you forgot.

marks.label: Email me a code
marks.text: Sends the code. The screen then asks for it.

marks.label: Back to sign in
marks.text: Returns to the sign-in screen.

steps.title: Forgot your password — the code
steps.text: Type the code from the email and a new password twice, then click “Set the password and sign in”.

marks.label: Sent
marks.text: Says the code is on its way (it only goes to an email that has an account).

marks.label: The code
marks.text: The 6 digits from the email.

marks.label: New password
marks.text: At least 8 characters.

marks.label: Again
marks.text: The same new password, to be sure it’s typed right.

marks.label: Set the password and sign in
marks.text: Saves the new password and opens your group’s data.

steps.title: Create an account
steps.text: Click “Create an account”. Type the first 3 letters of your organization and pick it from the names that appear, then your name, email and a password. The group’s admin approves you.

marks.label: Organization
marks.text: Type the first 3 letters of its name.

marks.label: Pick yours
marks.text: The groups whose name starts with those letters. Click yours; only these can be joined.

marks.label: Full name
marks.text: Your name, as the admin and the change history will show it.

marks.label: Email
marks.text: Your work email — the admin sees it, and the confirmation goes there.

marks.label: Password
marks.text: At least 8 characters.

marks.label: Again
marks.text: The same password again.

marks.label: Sign up
marks.text: Sends your request to join to the group’s admin.

marks.label: I have an account
marks.text: Back to the sign-in screen.

steps.title: Waiting for approval
steps.text: After Sign up the request goes to the group’s admin (in the app, and by email). When they approve it you get an email: confirm your address from it, then sign in.

marks.label: What happens now
marks.text: “Waiting for approval”. (Someone the admin already added is told to confirm their email instead.)

marks.label: Who approves
marks.text: The group and its admin, and the next steps.

marks.label: Back to sign in
marks.text: The sign-in screen, with your email filled in.

steps.title: Signing in before approval
steps.text: Until the admin approves, the sign-in screen reminds you of your request, and signing in says the account isn’t ready yet.

marks.label: Your request
marks.text: Which group you asked to join, and what to do once approved.

marks.label: Not ready yet
marks.text: Why signing in didn’t work yet.

steps.title: Signed in, but in no group
steps.text: An account that isn’t in a group yet (say, its admin removed it) can ask to join from here.

marks.label: Not in a group
marks.text: You’re signed in, but no group has you yet.

marks.label: Signed in as
marks.text: The account you’re signed in with, and what to do.

marks.label: Organization
marks.text: Type the first 3 letters of its name …

marks.label: Pick it
marks.text: … and click it.

marks.label: Full name
marks.text: Your name for the admin.

marks.label: Ask to join
marks.text: Sends the request to the group’s admin.

marks.label: Check again
marks.text: Once the admin approves, this opens the group.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in screen.

steps.title: The maintainer
steps.text: The maintainer (who looks after the shared database for every company) signs in here too. Each company is a group with one admin; the maintainer makes the groups and names their admins.

marks.label: The maintainer
marks.text: Signed in as the maintainer, in no group of their own.

marks.label: Ask to join a group
marks.text: A maintainer can also ask to join a group, like anyone in no group.

marks.label: A group
marks.text: Each group, its admin (“hasn’t signed in yet” until they do) and how many people it has.

marks.label: New admin…
marks.text: Makes someone else the group’s admin. The old admin stays in the group as an editor.

marks.label: New group
marks.text: The company’s name.

marks.label: Its admin’s email
marks.text: The person who will run the group.

marks.label: Admin’s name
marks.text: Their full name.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Makes the group. Its admin then creates an account (Create an account → the group’s name) and needs no approval — only to confirm the email.

marks.label: Check again
marks.text: Opens the group, once the maintainer is in one.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in screen.

topics.title: The admin’s first sign-in
topics.intro: The group starts empty: its admin uploads the starting data from their own computer.

steps.title: Someone asks to join
steps.text: When people are waiting to join, the admin’s app shows them as soon as it opens (they also got an email). Approve or turn down each one.

marks.label: Who asks
marks.text: Their name, email and when they asked.

marks.label: Turn down
marks.text: They get an email saying so.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: They get an email to confirm their address, then join as an editor. (Make them view only in Members and codes.)

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Decide later: the request waits (the menu’s “Asking to join” opens it again).

steps.title: Approved
steps.text: Approved: the person confirms their email from the link they get, then signs in.

marks.label: Done
marks.text: What happens next for them.

steps.title: An empty group
steps.text: A new group has no data. The banner offers the upload; nothing on this computer is used until you do it.

marks.label: No data yet
marks.text: The group is empty (a member who isn’t the admin is told the admin brings the starting data).

marks.label: Upload this computer’s data
marks.text: Opens the upload.

marks.label: You
marks.text: Who is signed in, and their role. Click it for the menu.

steps.title: Upload this computer’s data
steps.text: The loans, properties, their documents and chats on this computer become the group’s starting data. Nothing on this computer changes.

marks.label: What goes up
marks.text: How many loans, properties and documents, and how big the files are.

marks.label: From a backup file
marks.text: Upload a backup file (Data → Back up to a file…, from any computer) instead.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Kept in the change history.

marks.label: Not now
marks.text: Closes; the group stays empty.

marks.label: Upload
marks.text: Sends it, file by file, then opens the group’s data.

steps.title: The group’s data
steps.text: Uploaded: the group has the data. Everyone in the group sees the same, and changes reach every open app by themselves. (If the screen still says “No loans yet”, click Whole Portfolio.)

marks.label: Online
marks.text: Green: online, live with the group. Blue: a change of yours isn’t saved yet. Amber: offline.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: The whole group’s portfolio.

marks.label: The group’s loans
marks.text: The same for everyone in the group.

topics.title: The cloud chip and its menu
topics.intro: The chip in the title bar shows who is signed in; its menu has the group’s screens.

steps.title: The menu (admin)
steps.text: Click the chip. An admin sees every screen; an editor or a viewer sees only the change history and Sign out.

marks.label: The chip
marks.text: Name · role; “offline”, how many changes wait for you and how many people ask to join, when there are.

marks.label: The group
marks.text: The group, you, your role, and online (live) or offline (the last picture of the data).

marks.label: Requests
marks.text: Changes members asked you to approve.

marks.label: Asking to join
marks.text: People who asked to join.

marks.label: Members and codes
marks.text: Who is in the group and who can edit; your approval and offline codes.

marks.label: Daily backups
marks.text: Put the group’s data back as it was on a day.

marks.label: Start the group over…
marks.text: Removes all the group’s data, to upload the starting data again (asks you to type the group’s name). Before the first upload this is “Upload this computer’s data”.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change: who, when, why.

marks.label: Groups
marks.text: Only the maintainer: every group and its admin.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in screen. Changes not saved yet are dropped (it asks first).

topics.title: Saving a change, with a reason
topics.intro: Every change waits in a bar until you say why; then it is saved for everyone.

steps.title: Not saved yet
steps.text: Change anything (here a loan’s lender): the bar at the bottom lists what isn’t saved yet. Type why, then click Save (or press Enter).

marks.label: Not saved yet
marks.text: Your change is only on this computer until you save it.

marks.label: What changed
marks.text: The changes waiting (hover for the full list).

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Required — kept in the change history with your name.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves for everyone in the group.

marks.label: Undo
marks.text: Drops your changes; the data goes back to how it was.

steps.title: A member’s change waits for you
steps.text: A member who changes what the admin changed needs the admin’s approval: their request pops up in the admin’s app.

marks.label: Who and when
marks.text: The member who asked, and when.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, now, and their change.

marks.label: Turn down
marks.text: Asks for an optional note for them; nothing changes.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Their change takes effect for everyone.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Decide later (menu → Requests).

topics.title: Members and codes (the admin)
topics.intro: Who is in the group and what they can do, and the admin’s two codes.

steps.title: Members and codes
steps.text: Menu → Members and codes. People join by asking from the sign-in screen; here you set what each can do, or remove them.

marks.label: The admin
marks.text: The group’s one admin.

marks.label: Can
marks.text: Editor (can change data) or View only. It takes effect in their app at once.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes them out of the group (it asks first). Their app says so.

marks.label: Not signed in yet
marks.text: Approved, but hasn’t confirmed the email and signed in yet.

marks.label: Approval code
marks.text: Typed on a member’s screen to approve on the spot a change to what you changed.

marks.label: Offline code
marks.text: Lets you keep changing data on your own computer with no connection.

marks.label: Save the codes
marks.text: At least 6 characters each; an empty box keeps that code as it is.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

topics.title: Change history
topics.intro: Every change to the group’s data: who made it, when, and why.

steps.title: Change history
steps.text: Menu → Change history. Newest first; type in the box to find a name, a property or a reason.

marks.label: Find
marks.text: Shows only the changes with these words.

marks.label: When
marks.text: Date and time of the change.

marks.label: Who
marks.text: Who made it — and who approved it, for a member’s change the admin approved. “The app” for the app’s own work.

marks.label: Approved by
marks.text: A member’s change the admin approved names them both.

marks.label: What
marks.text: The property or loan, and the field.

marks.label: Before
marks.text: The value before.

marks.label: After
marks.text: The value after.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: The reason typed when it was saved.

marks.label: Older changes
marks.text: Loads the next 200 older changes.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

topics.title: Daily backups (the admin)
topics.intro: A backup of the group’s data is taken every day and kept 30 days.

steps.title: The backups
steps.text: Menu → Daily backups: one line per day.

marks.label: Put this day back
marks.text: The group’s data goes back to how it was that day, for everyone (asks why first).

marks.label: Empty
marks.text: Taken before the group had data — nothing to put back.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

steps.title: Putting a day back
steps.text: Type why and click “Put it back”. Every change it makes is in the change history with your reason.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Required; kept in the change history.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Put it back
marks.text: Puts the day back for everyone.

topics.title: Groups (the maintainer)
topics.intro: The maintainer sees every group from the menu too, when they are also in a group.

steps.title: Groups
steps.text: Menu → Groups (only the maintainer has it): every group, its admin and how many people; and a new group.

marks.label: A group
marks.text: The group, its admin and how many people.

marks.label: New admin…
marks.text: Makes someone else its admin; the old admin stays as an editor.

marks.label: New group
marks.text: The company’s name.

marks.label: Its admin’s email
marks.text: Who will run it.

marks.label: Admin’s full name
marks.text: Their name.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Makes the group; its admin then creates an account and only confirms the email.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

topics.title: Offline
topics.intro: With no connection the app keeps the last picture of the group’s data, view only.

steps.title: Offline — view only
steps.text: When the shared database can’t be reached, a banner says so and the chip turns amber. You can look at everything; changes can’t be saved until the connection is back — it reconnects by itself.

marks.label: Offline
marks.text: The chip says “offline” (amber dot).

marks.label: The banner
marks.text: What offline means: the last picture of the data, view only.

marks.label: Use my offline code
marks.text: Only the admin: keep changing data while offline.

steps.title: The offline code
steps.text: The admin types the offline code (set in Members and codes): changes are kept on this computer, each with its reason, and go up when the connection is back.

marks.label: Offline code
marks.text: The code you set in Members and codes.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Stay view only.

marks.label: Unlock
marks.text: You can change data offline; the banner says how many changes wait to go up.

topics.title: As an editor, and view only
topics.intro: What a member who isn’t the admin sees.

steps.title: The admin’s approval is needed
steps.text: An editor (here Eddie) changes what the admin changed: Save asks for the admin’s approval. The admin can type the approval code right there, or Eddie sends it to them.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, its value now, and the change.

marks.label: Approval code
marks.text: The admin types their code here (on Eddie’s screen) to approve it now.

marks.label: Undo my change
marks.text: Drops it.

marks.label: Send to the admin
marks.text: It pops up in the admin’s app. The current value stays until they approve; you get a note when they decide.

marks.label: Approve with the code
marks.text: Saves at once with the admin’s code.

steps.title: The editor’s menu
steps.text: A member’s menu has the change history and Sign out.

marks.label: Editor
marks.text: Eddie · Editor.

marks.label: The group
marks.text: The group, who you are and your role, online or offline.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change: who, when, why.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in screen.

steps.title: View only
steps.text: Someone the admin made view only sees everything in the group but can’t change it: a change they try is refused and the screen goes back.

marks.label: View only
marks.text: Vera · View only.

marks.label: The banner
marks.text: View only — you can see everything in the group but not change it.
